rule_based.label: Based on data, not yet reviewed by agents
rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: No operator has a clear line of sight to an identified site from here. Least obstructed: O2, a site 5.7 km south-east (inferred from crowd-sourced data), with terrain 135 m above the line.

limitations: Sites are approximate and antenna heights are assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level, not exact for this address.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

critiques.reason: Four line-of-sight computations [los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone] show terrain rising above the direct line to every operator's nearest site, with assumed antenna heights of 25 m [los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone]. Terrain rises 258 m above the line for EE [los_ee], 135 m for O2 [los_o2], 258 m for Three [los_three], and 291 m for Vodafone [los_vodafone]. The network_comparison item confirms no operator has a clear line of sight. The opposing evidence [speed_neighbours] is weak (only 2 tests in neighbouring cells) and shows some signal exists nearby, which is consistent with 'weakened, not necessarily lost'.

The nearest identified mast is 3.8 km away (Vodafone) [nearest_site][los_vodafone] and O2's nearest is 5.7 km [los_o2]; operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data (moderate reliability). Distance is a plausible contributing factor, especially in combination with terrain blocking. Confidence appropriately reflects the moderate evidence.

A Met Office yellow wind warning and forecast gusts up to 81.4 km/h [weather][met_office_warnings] could explain current or recent degradation. The evidence is weak (forecast sample) and the belief correctly limits its scope to current/recent effects. No speed_trend or historical speed data exists to determine whether poor service is long-standing, so the time pattern is unknown and no downgrade is warranted. Confidence matches the weak evidence. [met_office_warnings][weather]

No Ookla speed tests exist in this cell or within 1 km [speed_cell][speed_1km], neighbouring cells provide only 2 tests [speed_neighbours], and only three operators have sites within 5 km [operators_5km]. The evidence supports the conclusion that the exact point-level cause cannot be confirmed. Confidence is appropriate.
